title: iCloud Drive files
whyItMatters: iCloud Drive holds the user's documents and app data, including Desktop and Documents when syncing is on. Signing out does not delete local copies.
source: Apple support and macOS forensics: iCloud Drive content lives in ~/Library/Mobile Documents - https://www.macforensics.app/en/artifacts/cloud-storage-clients
notes: Online-only files appear as 0-byte placeholders; vacate counts metadata and never hydrates or downloads anything. App-specific iCloud folders are included.

cleanup.exportFirst: Copy every file you need from the iCloud Drive folder in Finder to a drive you keep before removing the local copies.
cleanup.signOut: In System Settings open your Apple Account and turn iCloud Drive off, so this Mac stops syncing the account's files.
steps: Copy the files you need to a drive you keep.
Turn iCloud Drive off for this Mac and confirm that Finder no longer shows the folder.
Delete the Mobile Documents folder named in the plan, then empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Local copies of iCloud Drive files are gone. Anything still in the account can be downloaded again on another device.
